nonblocking_findings: F12 [Nit] review-b: No committed test covers F11. At role base 3059e3fa the suite showed 5 failures and 24 passes (jr-green-d0f755c8.log:23). The scanner of that commit still built strings one character at a time. So the 24 passing tests cannot detect that defect. Rationale: a 4 MiB string value with `--max-old-space-size=64` aborted the 0019518e gate (SIGABRT after 1285 ms). The committed gate gave exit 0 in 48 ms. The same pair held at 8 MiB with caps of 64 MB and 96 MB, and at 12 MiB with a cap of 96 MB. A test of this kind runs in about 100 ms. Disposition: note. Optional: add a Red case that spawns the gate with that heap cap on a 4 MiB document and expects exit 0.

F13 [Nit] review-b: `decodedKey` (scripts/audit-gate.mjs:107-113) returns the raw token when `JSON.parse` throws. A scanner that must fail closed is better if the error reaches the try/catch in `main` (:208-212), which gives exit 2. The catch cannot fire for valid JSON, because every token comes from a document that already parsed. Rationale: I found no input that reaches it. The differential run on 36000 documents, the 46 end-to-end probes, and the depth sweeps gave 0 false passes. The sweeps used steps of 1 over depths 4900 to 5200 (objects) and 5300 to 5600 (arrays). A stack overflow inside `JSON.parse` could be swallowed there. All 602 escape-spelled duplicate documents there exited 2. Disposition: note. Optional: remove the try/catch, or rethrow a RangeError.

End-to-end probes on the committed gate used --input on a /tmp file and an 8 s guard. All 46 cases matched, with 0 mismatches. 21 duplicate documents exit 2 with only `audit unavailable` on stderr. They cover the plain duplicate and an escaped letter in high and in critical. They also cover hex case, a slash escape, a lone surrogate, and an astral character against its surrogate pair. They also cover an escaped quote, backslash, control character, and NUL. They end with a duplicate advisory id, a duplicate top-level metadata key, a duplicate advisories key, and a duplicate severity inside an advisory. 12 documents with a duplicate in or under an array exit 2 in 21 to 24 ms. None hangs. 6 tokenizer traps behave as expected. They hold a duplicate-looking object inside a string, an escaped backslash or quote at a string end, and braces inside keys. 7 guards exit 0. They hold sibling objects, different depths, key case, composed against decomposed e-acute, different escapes of different letters, empty containers, and heavy white space.

Differential run: the committed scanner function, cut from scripts/audit-gate.mjs, ran in a worker thread with an 80 ms watchdog for each document. Two oracles judged each document. One was the generator, which knows the decoded duplicates by construction. The other was the Python json module with an object_pairs_hook (python3 -I). Phase 1 used the same 9000 documents as round 3. It gave 1227 duplicates detected, 7773 clean accepted, 0 false passes, 0 false positives, and 0 hangs. The 0019518e scanner gave 662 false passes and 218 hangs on these documents. Phase 2 used an extended generator (depth 6, long keys, NUL, U+2028, BOM, control characters, and escapes in string values) on 12000 documents. It gave 3754 duplicates detected (2515 raw and 1239 escape-only), 8246 clean accepted, and 0 false passes, false positives, or hangs. Phase 3 used a duplicate-dense, array-heavy generator on 15000 documents. It gave 8751 duplicates detected (8181 raw and 570 escape-only), 6249 clean accepted, and 0 false passes, false positives, or hangs. Over all 36000 documents the counts were 13732 detected and 22268 clean. Python disagreed with the generator on 17 documents in phase 1 and on 17 in phase 2. Each of those writes one key with only one half of a surrogate pair escaped. Python reads two code points, and JavaScript reads one string. The JavaScript rule is the right one for the gate. No disagreement is unexplained.

Deep nesting on the committed gate: a clean document with one extra field n levels deep gave exit 0 up to 5004 levels for objects. Arrays gave exit 0 up to 5439 levels. Beyond those depths the gate gave exit 2 with only `audit unavailable`. The sweep covered depths 3000 to 9000 in steps of 20 for six document types, and steps of 1 around both thresholds. Every duplicate document exited 2 at every depth. This holds for raw and escape-spelled duplicates at the bottom of objects and of arrays (301 of 301 for each type). It includes 602 escape-spelled documents at step 1 around the thresholds. No exit outside 0 and 2 occurred. At 20000, 100000, and 1,000,000 levels, five document types each gave exit 2 in at most 232 ms.

A duplicate at the end of a 60 MiB document, plain or escape-spelled, gave exit 2 in 0.33 s with 177996 KB. One million duplicates in one object gave exit 2 in 0.25 s. At 0019518e the 10 MiB string took 0.66 s with 538816 KB. The 40 MiB string took 3.37 s with 1609376 KB. The 100 MiB string aborted (exit 134, 2135220 KB).

Mutation check of the Red r3 documents against the committed function text: removing key decoding (`return JSON.parse(raw)` becomes `return raw`) fails 4 documents. These are the four escape cases. Setting `found` never fails all 5 duplicate documents. Restoring the early return alone, removing both progress guards alone, and making the colon skip unconditional each fail 0 documents. Restoring the early return and removing both guards together makes the in-array document hang, as the 0019518e loop did. The two defenses are redundant for that document. The progress guards cannot fire on valid JSON, so they are defense in depth. No test can detect the loss of one defense alone, which is acceptable.
